doc.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024

title: Transcriptions of his solos
summary: Rowe asks about transcribed solos; a Michigan saxophonist transcribed ten of his solos and Margitza checked them.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Nice description. I think you just used the term “breaking with tonality.” I hope I’m quoting you correctly. And it makes me think about — I was looking at some of your transcribed solos on line. First of all have you looked at your transcribed solos on line?
Solos that I have done of other people?
Yeah. And other people have transcribed them.
Oh you mean some people have transcribed my playing?

Oh yeah because there are some transcriptions that I did of other players that are out there as well. Yes actually, there’s a book that was out a while ago and the person who did the transcriptions, he’s actually a fine saxophonist from Michigan, John Wojciehowski. He actually sent me, I think there are like ten solos in this book, to edit them, to make sure that they were correct.
How do you know they’re correct?
Well I can kind of tell just by reading through them and if I wasn’t sure I would listen to the recording.
